title: 1-Bit Full Adder Circuit
summary: A Full Adder adds three 1-bit binary inputs: A, B, and Carry-In (Cin). It produces two outputs: Sum (S) and Carry-Out (Cout).

images.title: Full Adder Block Diagram
images.caption: Inputs A, B, Cin and Outputs Sum, Cout.

images.title: Gate Schematic
images.caption: Full Adder using 2 XOR (7486), 2 AND (7408), and 1 OR (7432).

working_principle: Full Adder logic: Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin, Cout = (A·B) + (Cin·(A⊕B)). It cascades to form multi-bit parallel adders.
applications: N-bit Ripple Carry Adders in Processors
advantages: Supports Carry-In for cascading multi-bit addition
Can be built from 2 Half Adders and 1 OR gate
disadvantages: Ripple carry propagation delay scales linearly with N bits (O(N))
common_mistakes: Miswiring the OR gate combining the two Half Adder carry outputs.
quick_notes: Requires 9 NAND gates to synthesize with Universal Gates.

viva_questions.q: How many gates are required to build a Full Adder using basic gates?
viva_questions.a: 2 XOR gates, 2 AND gates, and 1 OR gate.

viva_questions.q: What is the difference between a Half Adder and a Full Adder?
viva_questions.a: A Half Adder accepts 2 inputs (A, B), while a Full Adder accepts 3 inputs (A, B, Cin).

interview_questions.q: How many 2:1 Multiplexers are needed to build a Full Adder?
interview_questions.a: 2 MUXes for Sum and 2 MUXes for Cout (Total 4 MUXes).
